payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_cli.py::test_a_spec_whose_retired_first_is_queued_at_base_refuses_before_the_cell_starts stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/cli.py. The claim was '`saffron cell` refuses a spec whose `retired_first` names a spec still queued in `.saffron/specs/` at `base_sha`, before any cell starts. It exits 1 and writes no task row. Its one line starts with the spec id, says `refused` and names the queued id. That base also holds a file in `done/` that does not parse, and the line carries the text `could not be read as a spec`. The working copy has the queued spec moved to `done/`, uncommitted. The same spec, with that id retired at `base_sha` and queued again in the working copy, reaches the cell. On a repo with no `.saffron` at `base_sha`, where the export raises `GitError`, the same spec exits 2, the code a setup failure takes, with no task row and no cell. Its one line starts with the spec id, names the failed read of `done/` at `base_sha`, and never says `not retired`.'. Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_cli.py::test_a_spec_whose_retired_first_cannot_be_checked_exits_as_a_setup_failure, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
